answer: Locking a refundable stake before an agent can earn makes fake identities expensive: a Sybil farmer must fund every copy, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught copying or lying. Like a canyon that admits only one river at a time, the stake bottleneck lets one attacker afford a handful of accounts, not thousands — a lone knoll cannot pretend to be a mountain range. Honest agents get their stake back at dawn of each settlement window, so the cost lands only on cheaters.
